# opys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/opys/0.10.1/opys/

## Expand description

opys — a file-based inventory of typed markdown documents: one markdown file
per document, with YAML frontmatter, stable IDs, tags, configurable types,
test plans, and a `verify` gate for CI.

The binary is a thin wrapper around [ run](https://docs.rs/fn.run.html). The modules are public so the
crate can be used as a library.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use error::`- [OpysError](https://docs.rs/error/enum.OpysError.html);
- `pub use error::`- [Result](https://docs.rs/error/type.Result.html);
- `pub use frontmatter::`- [Frontmatter](https://docs.rs/frontmatter/struct.Frontmatter.html);
- `pub use project::`- [Project](https://docs.rs/project/struct.Project.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [body](https://docs.rs/body/index.html)
- Parsing of the markdown body: title, sections, and checklist items.
- [cli](https://docs.rs/cli/index.html)
- Command-line interface (clap derive).
- [commands](https://docs.rs/commands/index.html)
- Subcommand implementations. Each `run`takes the invocation`Ctx`
- [config](https://docs.rs/config/index.html)
- Shared field-spec types used by the universal config (`opys.toml`). See`crate::project_config`
- [doc](https://docs.rs/doc/index.html)
- A single inventory document in memory — the unified representation of every
configured type. This collapses the former `Feature`and`WorkItem`, which were identical`{path, frontmatter, body, title}`structs; a doc’s*type*is derived from its ID prefix via the config, not stored here.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- [file_](https://docs.rs/file_refs/index.html)- refs
- Scan source files for textual references to document ids.
- [frontmatter](https://docs.rs/frontmatter/index.html)
- Frontmatter parsing and canonical serialization.
- [links](https://docs.rs/links/index.html)
- Cross-reference auto-sync: keep every doc’s `references`map bidirectional and title-fresh, and rewrite bare`FEAT-XXXX`/`WI-XXXX`mentions in body prose into readable markdown links. Run by`sync`after every mutating command.
- [mdprism](https://docs.rs/mdprism/index.html)
- mdprism — markdown ⇄ data, via a template
- [palette](https://docs.rs/palette/index.html)
- Configurable presentation rules for the TUI (`[palette]`in opys.toml).
- [project](https://docs.rs/project/index.html)
- The project: `opys.toml`at the project root (found by searching upward), plus the inventory base it points at (default`opys/`, holding the document files and`_retired.txt`).
- [project_](https://docs.rs/project_config/index.html)- config
- The universal typed-document config (`opys.toml`) — the sole source of truth for the engine.
- [refs](https://docs.rs/refs/index.html)
- The uniform `references`field: an ID->title map linking a feature or work item to other features and work items.
- [rules](https://docs.rs/rules/index.html)
- The conditional validation-rules engine for the universal config.
- [templates](https://docs.rs/templates/index.html)
- String templates emitted by `opys init`and`opys agent-rules`.
- [tui](https://docs.rs/tui/index.html)
- Interactive terminal UI for opys — a live board over the inventory that updates as documents change on disk.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Ctx](https://docs.rs/struct.Ctx.html)
- Shared invocation context: where the inventory lives and global flags.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [run](https://docs.rs/fn.run.html)
- Execute a parsed CLI invocation, returning the process exit code.

# stderrlog - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/stderrlog/0.6.0/target-redirect/stderrlog/

## Expand description

A simple logger to provide semantics similar to what is expected of most UNIX utilities by logging to stderr and the higher the verbosity the higher the log level. It supports the ability to provide timestamps at different granularities. As well as colorizing the different log levels.

[§](https://docs.rs#simple-use-case)Simple Use Case

```
use log::*;
fn main() {
    stderrlog::new().module(module_path!()).init().unwrap();
    error!("some failure");
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#structopt-example)StructOpt Example

```
use log::*;
use structopt::StructOpt;
/// A StructOpt example
#[derive(StructOpt, Debug)]
#[structopt()]
struct Opt {
    /// Silence all output
    #[structopt(short = "q", long = "quiet")]
    quiet: bool,
    /// Verbose mode (-v, -vv, -vvv, etc)
    #[structopt(short = "v", long = "verbose", parse(from_occurrences))]
    verbose: usize,
    /// Timestamp (sec, ms, ns, none)
    #[structopt(short = "t", long = "timestamp")]
    ts: Option<stderrlog::Timestamp>,
}
fn main() {
    let opt = Opt::from_args();
    stderrlog::new()
        .module(module_path!())
        .quiet(opt.quiet)
        .verbosity(opt.verbose)
        .timestamp(opt.ts.unwrap_or(stderrlog::Timestamp::Off))
        .init()
        .unwrap();
    trace!("trace message");
    debug!("debug message");
    info!("info message");
    warn!("warn message");
    error!("error message");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#docopt-example)docopt Example

```
use log::*;
use docopt::Docopt;
use serde::Deserialize;
const USAGE: &'static str = "
Usage: program [-q] [-v...]
";
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct Args {
    flag_q: bool,
    flag_v: usize,
}
fn main() {
    let args: Args = Docopt::new(USAGE)
                            .and_then(|d| d.deserialize())
                            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.exit());
    stderrlog::new()
            .module(module_path!())
            .quiet(args.flag_q)
            .timestamp(stderrlog::Timestamp::Second)
            .verbosity(args.flag_v)
            .init()
            .unwrap();
    trace!("trace message");
    debug!("debug message");
    info!("info message");
    warn!("warn message");
    error!("error message");
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#clap-example)clap Example

```
use clap::{Arg, App, crate_version};
use log::*;
use std::str::FromStr;
fn main() {
    let m = App::new("stderrlog example")
        .version(crate_version!())
        .arg(Arg::with_name("verbosity")
             .short('v')
             .takes_value(true)
             .multiple(true)
             .help("Increase message verbosity"))
        .arg(Arg::with_name("quiet")
             .short('q')
             .help("Silence all output"))
        .arg(Arg::with_name("timestamp")
             .short('t')
             .help("prepend log lines with a timestamp")
             .takes_value(true)
             .possible_values(&["none", "sec", "ms", "ns"]))
        .get_matches();
    let verbose = m.occurrences_of("verbosity") as usize;
    let quiet = m.is_present("quiet");
    let ts = m.value_of("timestamp").map(|v| {
        stderrlog::Timestamp::from_str(v).unwrap_or_else(|_| {
            clap::Error::raw(clap::ErrorKind::InvalidValue, "invalid value for 'timestamp'").exit()
        })
    }).unwrap_or(stderrlog::Timestamp::Off);
    stderrlog::new()
        .module(module_path!())
        .quiet(quiet)
        .verbosity(verbose)
        .timestamp(ts)
        .init()
        .unwrap();
    trace!("trace message");
    debug!("debug message");
    info!("info message");
    warn!("warn message");
    error!("error message");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#log-compatibility)`log` Compatibility

The 0.5.x versions of `stderrlog` aim to provide compatibility with
applications using `log` >= 0.4.11.

[§](https://docs.rs#rust-compatibility)Rust Compatibility

`stderrlog` is serious about backwards compat. `stderrlog`
pins the minimum required version of Rust in the CI build.
Bumping the minimum version of Rust is a minor breaking
change and requires a minor version to be bumped.

The minimum supported Rust version for this release is 1.48.0.

[§](https://docs.rs#module-level-logging)Module Level Logging

`stderrlog` has the ability to limit the components which can log.
Many crates use [log](https://docs.rs/log/*/log/) but you may not
want their output in your application. For example
[hyper](https://docs.rs/hyper/*/hyper/) makes heavy use of log but
when your application receives `-vvvvv` to enable the `trace!()`
messages you don’t want the output of `hyper`’s `trace!()` level.

To support this `stderrlog` includes a `module()` method allowing
you to specify the modules that are allowed to log. The examples
above use the `module_path!()` macro to enable logging only for
the binary itself but none of its dependencies. To enable logging
from extra crates just add another call to `module()` with the
name of the crate. To enable logging for only a module within
that crate specify `crate::module` to `module()`. crates and
modules will be named the same way would would include them in
source code with `use` (e.g. `some-crate` would be `some_crate`).

For a good example of how the module level logging works see the
[large-example
crate](https://github.com/cardoe/stderrlog-rs/tree/master/examples/large-example)
under examples, you’ll want to run the
following binaries to see all the examples:

- `cargo run --bin large-example --`
- `cargo run --bin another --`
- `cargo run --bin yet --`

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

`stderrlog` has the following default crate features, which can be disabled
to reduce the number of dependencies:

- `timestamps`: Provides support for log timestamp prefixes (uses the- `chrono`crate).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [StdErr](https://docs.rs/struct.StdErrLog.html)- Log
- Data specific to this logger

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Color](https://docs.rs/enum.ColorChoice.html)- Choice
- ColorChoice represents the color preferences of an end user.
- [LogLevel](https://docs.rs/enum.LogLevelNum.html)- Num
- [Timestamp](https://docs.rs/enum.Timestamp.html)
- State of the timestamping in the logger.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [new](https://docs.rs/fn.new.html)
- creates a new stderr logger

[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!         .init()
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//!         .unwrap();
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!     trace!("trace message");
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//!     debug!("debug message");
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!     info!("info message");
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//!     warn!("warn message");
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//!     error!("error message");
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! }
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! ```
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//!
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! ## docopt Example
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//!
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//! ```rust
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! use log::*;
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! use docopt::Docopt;
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! use serde::Deserialize;
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//!
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! const USAGE: &'static str = "
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! Usage: program [-q] [-v...]
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! ";
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//!
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! struct Args {
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//!     flag_q: bool,
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//!     flag_v: usize,
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! }
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//!
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! fn main() {
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//!     let args: Args = Docopt::new(USAGE)
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//!                             .and_then(|d| d.deserialize())
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//!                             .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.exit());
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//!
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//!     stderrlog::new()
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//!             .module(module_path!())
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//!             .quiet(args.flag_q)
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//!             .timestamp(stderrlog::Timestamp::Second)
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//!             .verbosity(args.flag_v)
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//!             .init()
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//!             .unwrap();
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//!     trace!("trace message");
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//!     debug!("debug message");
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//!     info!("info message");
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//!     warn!("warn message");
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//!     error!("error message");
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//!
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//!     // ...
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//! }
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//! ```
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//!
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//! # clap Example
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//!
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//! ```
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//! use clap::{Arg, App, crate_version};
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//! use log::*;
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//! use std::str::FromStr;
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//!
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//! fn main() {
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//!     let m = App::new("stderrlog example")
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//!         .version(crate_version!())
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//!         .arg(Arg::with_name("verbosity")
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//!              .short('v')
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//!              .takes_value(true)
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//!              .multiple(true)
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//!              .help("Increase message verbosity"))
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//!         .arg(Arg::with_name("quiet")
[126](https://docs.rs#126)//!              .short('q')
[127](https://docs.rs#127)//!              .help("Silence all output"))
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//!         .arg(Arg::with_name("timestamp")
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//!              .short('t')
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//!              .help("prepend log lines with a timestamp")
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//!              .takes_value(true)
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//!              .possible_values(&["none", "sec", "ms", "ns"]))
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//!         .get_matches();
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//!
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//!     let verbose = m.occurrences_of("verbosity") as usize;
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//!     let quiet = m.is_present("quiet");
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//!     let ts = m.value_of("timestamp").map(|v| {
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//!         stderrlog::Timestamp::from_str(v).unwrap_or_else(|_| {
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//!             clap::Error::raw(clap::ErrorKind::InvalidValue, "invalid value for 'timestamp'").exit()
[140](https://docs.rs#140)//!         })
[141](https://docs.rs#141)//!     }).unwrap_or(stderrlog::Timestamp::Off);
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//!
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//!     stderrlog::new()
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//!         .module(module_path!())
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//!         .quiet(quiet)
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//!         .verbosity(verbose)
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//!         .timestamp(ts)
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//!         .init()
[149](https://docs.rs#149)//!         .unwrap();
[150](https://docs.rs#150)//!     trace!("trace message");
[151](https://docs.rs#151)//!     debug!("debug message");
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//!     info!("info message");
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//!     warn!("warn message");
[154](https://docs.rs#154)//!     error!("error message");
[155](https://docs.rs#155)//! }
[156](https://docs.rs#156)//! ```
[157](https://docs.rs#157)//!
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//! ### `log` Compatibility
[159](https://docs.rs#159)//!
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//! The 0.5.x versions of `stderrlog` aim to provide compatibility with
[161](https://docs.rs#161)//! applications using `log` >= 0.4.11.
[162](https://docs.rs#162)//!
[163](https://docs.rs#163)//! ### Rust Compatibility
[164](https://docs.rs#164)//!
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//! `stderrlog` is serious about backwards compat. `stderrlog`
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//! pins the minimum required version of Rust in the CI build.
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//! Bumping the minimum version of Rust is a minor breaking
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//! change and requires a minor version to be bumped.
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//!
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//! The minimum supported Rust version for this release is 1.48.0.
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//!
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//! ### Module Level Logging
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//!
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//! `stderrlog` has the ability to limit the components which can log.
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//! Many crates use [log](https://docs.rs/log/*/log/) but you may not
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//! want their output in your application. For example
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//! [hyper](https://docs.rs/hyper/*/hyper/) makes heavy use of log but
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//! when your application receives `-vvvvv` to enable the `trace!()`
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//! messages you don't want the output of `hyper`'s `trace!()` level.
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//!
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//! To support this `stderrlog` includes a `module()` method allowing
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//! you to specify the modules that are allowed to log. The examples
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//! above use the `module_path!()` macro to enable logging only for
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//! the binary itself but none of its dependencies. To enable logging
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//! from extra crates just add another call to `module()` with the
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//! name of the crate. To enable logging for only a module within
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//! that crate specify `crate::module` to `module()`. crates and
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//! modules will be named the same way would would include them in
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//! source code with `use` (e.g. `some-crate` would be `some_crate`).
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//!
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//! For a good example of how the module level logging works see the
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//! [large-example
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//! crate](https://github.com/cardoe/stderrlog-rs/tree/master/examples/large-example)
[194](https://docs.rs#194)//! under examples, you'll want to run the
[195](https://docs.rs#195)//! following binaries to see all the examples:
[196](https://docs.rs#196)//!
[197](https://docs.rs#197)//! - `cargo run --bin large-example --`
[198](https://docs.rs#198)//! - `cargo run --bin another --`
[199](https://docs.rs#199)//! - `cargo run --bin yet --`
[200](https://docs.rs#200)//!
[201](https://docs.rs#201)//! ### Features
[202](https://docs.rs#202)//!
[203](https://docs.rs#203)//! `stderrlog` has the following default crate features, which can be disabled
[204](https://docs.rs#204)//! to reduce the number of dependencies:
[205](https://docs.rs#205)//!
[206](https://docs.rs#206)//! - `timestamps`: Provides support for log timestamp prefixes (uses the `chrono` crate).
[207](https://docs.rs#207)
[208](https://docs.rs#208)#[cfg(feature = "timestamps")]
[209](https://docs.rs#209)use chrono::Local;
[210](https://docs.rs#210)use is_terminal::IsTerminal;
[211](https://docs.rs#211)use log::{Level, LevelFilter, Log, Metadata, Record};
[212](https://docs.rs#212)use std::cell::RefCell;
[213](https://docs.rs#213)use std::fmt;
[214](https://docs.rs#214)use std::io::{self, Write};
[215](https://docs.rs#215)#[cfg(feature = "timestamps")]
[216](https://docs.rs#216)use std::str::FromStr;
[217](https://docs.rs#217)use termcolor::{Color, ColorSpec, StandardStream, WriteColor};
[218](https://docs.rs#218)
[219](https://docs.rs#219)pub use termcolor::ColorChoice;
[220](https://docs.rs#220)use thread_local::ThreadLocal;
[221](https://docs.rs#221)
[222](https://docs.rs#222)/// State of the timestamping in the logger.
[223](https://docs.rs#223)#[cfg(feature = "timestamps")]
[224](https://docs.rs#224)#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
[225](https://docs.rs#225)pub enum Timestamp {
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    /// Disable timestamping of log messages
[227](https://docs.rs#227)    Off,
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    /// Timestamp with second granularity
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    Second,
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    /// Timestamp with millisecond granularity
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    Millisecond,
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    /// Timestamp with microsecond granularity
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    Microsecond,
[234](https://docs.rs#234)    /// Timestamp with nanosecond granularity
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    Nanosecond,
[236](https://docs.rs#236)}
[237](https://docs.rs#237)
[238](https://docs.rs#238)/// Provides a quick conversion of the following:
[239](https://docs.rs#239)///
[240](https://docs.rs#240)/// - "sec" -> `Timestamp::Second`
[241](https://docs.rs#241)/// - "ms" -> `Timestamp::Millisecond`
[242](https://docs.rs#242)/// - "us" -> `Timestamp::Microsecond`
[243](https://docs.rs#243)/// - "ns" -> `Timestamp::Nanosecond`
[244](https://docs.rs#244)/// - "none" | "off" -> `Timestamp::Off`
[245](https://docs.rs#245)///
[246](https://docs.rs#246)/// This is provided as a helper for argument parsers
[247](https://docs.rs#247)#[cfg(feature = "timestamps")]
[248](https://docs.rs#248)impl FromStr for Timestamp {
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    type Err = String;
[250](https://docs.rs#250)
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
[252](https://docs.rs#252)        match s {
[253](https://docs.rs#253)            "ns" => Ok(Timestamp::Nanosecond),
[254](https://docs.rs#254)            "ms" => Ok(Timestamp::Millisecond),
[255](https://docs.rs#255)            "us" => Ok(Timestamp::Microsecond),
[256](https://docs.rs#256)            "sec" => Ok(Timestamp::Second),
[257](https://docs.rs#257)            "none" | "off" => Ok(Timestamp::Off),
[258](https://docs.rs#258)            _ => Err("invalid value".into()),
[259](https://docs.rs#259)        }
[260](https://docs.rs#260)    }
[261](https://docs.rs#261)}

[303](https://docs.rs#303)
[304](https://docs.rs#304)impl Log for StdErrLog {
[305](https://docs.rs#305)    fn enabled(&self, metadata: &Metadata) -> bool {
[306](https://docs.rs#306)        metadata.level() <= self.log_level_filter() && self.includes_module(metadata.target())
[307](https://docs.rs#307)    }
[308](https://docs.rs#308)
[309](https://docs.rs#309)    fn log(&self, record: &Record) {
[310](https://docs.rs#310)        // if logging isn't enabled for this level do a quick out
[311](https://docs.rs#311)        if !self.enabled(record.metadata()) {
[312](https://docs.rs#312)            return;
[313](https://docs.rs#313)        }
[314](https://docs.rs#314)
[315](https://docs.rs#315)        let writer = self
[316](https://docs.rs#316)            .writer
[317](https://docs.rs#317)            .get_or(|| RefCell::new(StandardStream::stderr(self.color_choice)));
[318](https://docs.rs#318)        let writer = writer.borrow_mut();
[319](https://docs.rs#319)        let mut writer = io::LineWriter::new(writer.lock());
[320](https://docs.rs#320)        let color = match record.metadata().level() {
[321](https://docs.rs#321)            Level::Error => Color::Red,
[322](https://docs.rs#322)            Level::Warn => Color::Yellow,
[323](https://docs.rs#323)            Level::Info => Color::Blue,
[324](https://docs.rs#324)            Level::Debug => Color::Cyan,
[325](https://docs.rs#325)            Level::Trace => Color::Magenta,
[326](https://docs.rs#326)        };
[327](https://docs.rs#327)        {
[328](https://docs.rs#328)            // A failure here indicates the stream closed. Do not panic.
[329](https://docs.rs#329)            writer
[330](https://docs.rs#330)                .get_mut()
[331](https://docs.rs#331)                .set_color(ColorSpec::new().set_fg(Some(color)))
[332](https://docs.rs#332)                .ok();
[333](https://docs.rs#333)        }
[334](https://docs.rs#334)
[335](https://docs.rs#335)        if self.show_module_names {
[336](https://docs.rs#336)            let _ = write!(writer, "{}: ", record.metadata().target());
[337](https://docs.rs#337)        }
[338](https://docs.rs#338)        #[cfg(feature = "timestamps")]
[339](https://docs.rs#339)        match self.timestamp {
[340](https://docs.rs#340)            Timestamp::Second => {
[341](https://docs.rs#341)                let fmt = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%:z";
[342](https://docs.rs#342)                let _ = write!(writer, "{} - ", Local::now().format(fmt));
[343](https://docs.rs#343)            }
[344](https://docs.rs#344)            Timestamp::Millisecond => {
[345](https://docs.rs#345)                let fmt = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%.3f%:z";
[346](https://docs.rs#346)                let _ = write!(writer, "{} - ", Local::now().format(fmt));
[347](https://docs.rs#347)            }
[348](https://docs.rs#348)            Timestamp::Microsecond => {
[349](https://docs.rs#349)                let fmt = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%.6f%:z";
[350](https://docs.rs#350)                let _ = write!(writer, "{} - ", Local::now().format(fmt));
[351](https://docs.rs#351)            }
[352](https://docs.rs#352)            Timestamp::Nanosecond => {
[353](https://docs.rs#353)                let fmt = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%.9f%:z";
[354](https://docs.rs#354)                let _ = write!(writer, "{} - ", Local::now().format(fmt));
[355](https://docs.rs#355)            }
[356](https://docs.rs#356)            Timestamp::Off => {}
[357](https://docs.rs#357)        }
[358](https://docs.rs#358)        if self.show_level {
[359](https://docs.rs#359)            let _ = write!(writer, "{} ", record.level());
[360](https://docs.rs#360)        }
[361](https://docs.rs#361)        writer.flush().ok();
[362](https://docs.rs#362)        {
[363](https://docs.rs#363)            // A failure here indicates the stream closed. Do not panic.
[364](https://docs.rs#364)            writer.get_mut().reset().ok();
[365](https://docs.rs#365)        }
[366](https://docs.rs#366)        let _ = writeln!(writer, "{}", record.args());
[367](https://docs.rs#367)    }
[368](https://docs.rs#368)
[369](https://docs.rs#369)    fn flush(&self) {
[370](https://docs.rs#370)        let writer = self
[371](https://docs.rs#371)            .writer
[372](https://docs.rs#372)            .get_or(|| RefCell::new(StandardStream::stderr(self.color_choice)));
[373](https://docs.rs#373)        let mut writer = writer.borrow_mut();
[374](https://docs.rs#374)        writer.flush().ok();
[375](https://docs.rs#375)    }
[376](https://docs.rs#376)}

[439](https://docs.rs#439)
[440](https://docs.rs#440)    /// Sets the verbosity level of messages that will be displayed

[442](https://docs.rs#442)    /// Values can be supplied as:

[502](https://docs.rs#502)    fn _module(&mut self, module: String) -> &mut StdErrLog {
[503](https://docs.rs#503)        // If Ok, the module was already found
[504](https://docs.rs#504)        if let Err(i) = self.modules.binary_search(&module) {
[505](https://docs.rs#505)            // If a super-module of the current module already exists, don't insert this module
[506](https://docs.rs#506)            if i == 0 || !is_submodule(&self.modules[i - 1], &module) {
[507](https://docs.rs#507)                // Remove any submodules of the module we're inserting
[508](https://docs.rs#508)                let submodule_count = self.modules[i..]
[509](https://docs.rs#509)                    .iter()
[510](https://docs.rs#510)                    .take_while(|possible_submodule| is_submodule(&module, possible_submodule))
[511](https://docs.rs#511)                    .count();
[512](https://docs.rs#512)                self.modules.drain(i..i + submodule_count);
[513](https://docs.rs#513)                self.modules.insert(i, module);
[514](https://docs.rs#514)            }
[515](https://docs.rs#515)        }
[516](https://docs.rs#516)        self
[517](https://docs.rs#517)    }
[518](https://docs.rs#518)
[519](https://docs.rs#519)    /// specify modules to allow to log to stderr
[520](https://docs.rs#520)    pub fn modules<T: Into<String>, I: IntoIterator<Item = T>>(
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        &mut self,
[522](https://docs.rs#522)        modules: I,
[523](https://docs.rs#523)    ) -> &mut StdErrLog {
[524](https://docs.rs#524)        for module in modules {
[525](https://docs.rs#525)            self.module(module);
[526](https://docs.rs#526)        }

[537](https://docs.rs#537)
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    fn includes_module(&self, module_path: &str) -> bool {
[539](https://docs.rs#539)        // If modules is empty, include all module paths
[540](https://docs.rs#540)        if self.modules.is_empty() {
[541](https://docs.rs#541)            return true;
[542](https://docs.rs#542)        }
[543](https://docs.rs#543)        // if a prefix of module_path is in `self.modules`, it must
[544](https://docs.rs#544)        // be located at the first location before
[545](https://docs.rs#545)        // where module_path would be.
[546](https://docs.rs#546)        match self
[547](https://docs.rs#547)            .modules
[548](https://docs.rs#548)            .binary_search_by(|module| module.as_str().cmp(module_path))
[549](https://docs.rs#549)        {
[550](https://docs.rs#550)            Ok(_) => {
[551](https://docs.rs#551)                // Found exact module: return true
[552](https://docs.rs#552)                true
[553](https://docs.rs#553)            }
[554](https://docs.rs#554)            Err(0) => {
[555](https://docs.rs#555)                // if there's no item which would be located before module_path, no prefix is there
[556](https://docs.rs#556)                false
[557](https://docs.rs#557)            }
[558](https://docs.rs#558)            Err(i) => is_submodule(&self.modules[i - 1], module_path),
[559](https://docs.rs#559)        }
[560](https://docs.rs#560)    }
[561](https://docs.rs#561)
[562](https://docs.rs#562)    /// sets the the logger as active
[563](https://docs.rs#563)    pub fn init(&mut self) -> Result<(), log::SetLoggerError> {
[564](https://docs.rs#564)        /* if the user is using auto color choices then
[565](https://docs.rs#565)         * detect if stderr is a tty, if it is continue
[566](https://docs.rs#566)         * otherwise turn off colors by default
[567](https://docs.rs#567)         */
[568](https://docs.rs#568)        self.color_choice = match self.color_choice {
[569](https://docs.rs#569)            ColorChoice::Auto => {
[570](https://docs.rs#570)                if io::stderr().is_terminal() {
[571](https://docs.rs#571)                    ColorChoice::Auto
[572](https://docs.rs#572)                } else {
[573](https://docs.rs#573)                    ColorChoice::Never
[574](https://docs.rs#574)                }
[575](https://docs.rs#575)            }
[576](https://docs.rs#576)            other => other,
[577](https://docs.rs#577)        };
[578](https://docs.rs#578)        log::set_max_level(self.log_level_filter());
[579](https://docs.rs#579)        log::set_boxed_logger(Box::new(self.clone()))
[580](https://docs.rs#580)    }

[593](https://docs.rs#593)
[594](https://docs.rs#594)fn is_submodule(parent: &str, possible_child: &str) -> bool {
[595](https://docs.rs#595)    // Treat as bytes, because we'll be doing slicing, and we only care about ':' chars
[596](https://docs.rs#596)    let parent = parent.as_bytes();
[597](https://docs.rs#597)    let possible_child = possible_child.as_bytes();
[598](https://docs.rs#598)
[599](https://docs.rs#599)    // a longer module path cannot be a parent of a shorter module path
[600](https://docs.rs#600)    if parent.len() > possible_child.len() {
[601](https://docs.rs#601)        return false;
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    }
[603](https://docs.rs#603)
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    // If the path up to the parent isn't the same as the child,
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    if parent != &possible_child[..parent.len()] {
[606](https://docs.rs#606)        return false;
[607](https://docs.rs#607)    }
[608](https://docs.rs#608)
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    // Either the path is exactly the same, or the sub module should have a "::" after
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    // the length of the parent path. This prevents things like 'a::bad' being considered
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    // a submodule of 'a::b'
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    parent.len() == possible_child.len()
[613](https://docs.rs#613)        || possible_child.get(parent.len()..parent.len() + 2) == Some(b"::")
[614](https://docs.rs#614)}
[615](https://docs.rs#615)

# ColorChoice in stderrlog - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/stderrlog/0.6.0/stderrlog/enum.ColorChoice.html

```
pub enum ColorChoice {
    Always,
    AlwaysAnsi,
    Auto,
    Never,
}
```
## Expand description

ColorChoice represents the color preferences of an end user.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Always)

### Always

Try very hard to emit colors. This includes emitting ANSI colors on Windows if the console API is unavailable.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AlwaysAnsi)

### AlwaysAnsi

AlwaysAnsi is like Always, except it never tries to use anything other than emitting ANSI color codes.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Auto)

### Auto

Try to use colors, but don’t force the issue. If the console isn’t
available on Windows, or if TERM=dumb, or if `NO_COLOR` is defined, for
example, then don’t use colors.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Never)

### Never

Never emit colors.

# stderrlog - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/stderrlog/latest/stderrlog/

## Expand description

A simple logger to provide semantics similar to what is expected of most UNIX utilities by logging to stderr and the higher the verbosity the higher the log level. It supports the ability to provide timestamps at different granularities. As well as colorizing the different log levels.

[§](https://docs.rs#simple-use-case)Simple Use Case

```
use log::*;
fn main() {
    stderrlog::new().module(module_path!()).init().unwrap();
    error!("some failure");
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#structopt-example)StructOpt Example

```
use log::*;
use structopt::StructOpt;
/// A StructOpt example
#[derive(StructOpt, Debug)]
#[structopt()]
struct Opt {
    /// Silence all output
    #[structopt(short = "q", long = "quiet")]
    quiet: bool,
    /// Verbose mode (-v, -vv, -vvv, etc)
    #[structopt(short = "v", long = "verbose", parse(from_occurrences))]
    verbose: usize,
    /// Timestamp (sec, ms, ns, none)
    #[structopt(short = "t", long = "timestamp")]
    ts: Option<stderrlog::Timestamp>,
}
fn main() {
    let opt = Opt::from_args();
    stderrlog::new()
        .module(module_path!())
        .quiet(opt.quiet)
        .verbosity(opt.verbose)
        .timestamp(opt.ts.unwrap_or(stderrlog::Timestamp::Off))
        .init()
        .unwrap();
    trace!("trace message");
    debug!("debug message");
    info!("info message");
    warn!("warn message");
    error!("error message");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#docopt-example)docopt Example

```
use log::*;
use docopt::Docopt;
use serde::Deserialize;
const USAGE: &'static str = "
Usage: program [-q] [-v...]
";
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct Args {
    flag_q: bool,
    flag_v: usize,
}
fn main() {
    let args: Args = Docopt::new(USAGE)
                            .and_then(|d| d.deserialize())
                            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.exit());
    stderrlog::new()
            .module(module_path!())
            .quiet(args.flag_q)
            .timestamp(stderrlog::Timestamp::Second)
            .verbosity(args.flag_v)
            .init()
            .unwrap();
    trace!("trace message");
    debug!("debug message");
    info!("info message");
    warn!("warn message");
    error!("error message");
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#clap-example)clap Example

```
use clap::{Arg, App, crate_version};
use log::*;
use std::str::FromStr;
fn main() {
    let m = App::new("stderrlog example")
        .version(crate_version!())
        .arg(Arg::with_name("verbosity")
             .short('v')
             .takes_value(true)
             .multiple(true)
             .help("Increase message verbosity"))
        .arg(Arg::with_name("quiet")
             .short('q')
             .help("Silence all output"))
        .arg(Arg::with_name("timestamp")
             .short('t')
             .help("prepend log lines with a timestamp")
             .takes_value(true)
             .possible_values(&["none", "sec", "ms", "ns"]))
        .get_matches();
    let verbose = m.occurrences_of("verbosity") as usize;
    let quiet = m.is_present("quiet");
    let ts = m.value_of("timestamp").map(|v| {
        stderrlog::Timestamp::from_str(v).unwrap_or_else(|_| {
            clap::Error::raw(clap::ErrorKind::InvalidValue, "invalid value for 'timestamp'").exit()
        })
    }).unwrap_or(stderrlog::Timestamp::Off);
    stderrlog::new()
        .module(module_path!())
        .quiet(quiet)
        .verbosity(verbose)
        .timestamp(ts)
        .init()
        .unwrap();
    trace!("trace message");
    debug!("debug message");
    info!("info message");
    warn!("warn message");
    error!("error message");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#log-compatibility)`log` Compatibility

The 0.5.x versions of `stderrlog` aim to provide compatibility with
applications using `log` >= 0.4.11.

[§](https://docs.rs#rust-compatibility)Rust Compatibility

`stderrlog` is serious about backwards compat. `stderrlog`
pins the minimum required version of Rust in the CI build.
Bumping the minimum version of Rust is a minor breaking
change and requires a minor version to be bumped.

The minimum supported Rust version for this release is 1.48.0.

[§](https://docs.rs#module-level-logging)Module Level Logging

`stderrlog` has the ability to limit the components which can log.
Many crates use [log](https://docs.rs/log/*/log/) but you may not
want their output in your application. For example
[hyper](https://docs.rs/hyper/*/hyper/) makes heavy use of log but
when your application receives `-vvvvv` to enable the `trace!()`
messages you don’t want the output of `hyper`’s `trace!()` level.

To support this `stderrlog` includes a `module()` method allowing
you to specify the modules that are allowed to log. The examples
above use the `module_path!()` macro to enable logging only for
the binary itself but none of its dependencies. To enable logging
from extra crates just add another call to `module()` with the
name of the crate. To enable logging for only a module within
that crate specify `crate::module` to `module()`. crates and
modules will be named the same way would would include them in
source code with `use` (e.g. `some-crate` would be `some_crate`).

For a good example of how the module level logging works see the
[large-example
crate](https://github.com/cardoe/stderrlog-rs/tree/master/examples/large-example)
under examples, you’ll want to run the
following binaries to see all the examples:

- `cargo run --bin large-example --`
- `cargo run --bin another --`
- `cargo run --bin yet --`

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

`stderrlog` has the following default crate features, which can be disabled
to reduce the number of dependencies:

- `timestamps`: Provides support for log timestamp prefixes (uses the- `chrono`crate).

# chrono 0.4.45 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/chrono/^0.4.10

[Chrono](https://docs.rs/chrono): Timezone-aware date and time handling

Chrono aims to provide all functionality needed to do correct operations on dates and times in the
[proleptic Gregorian calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proleptic_Gregorian_calendar):

- The `DateTime`
- Operations that may produce an invalid or ambiguous date and time return `Option`or`MappedLocalTime`
- Configurable parsing and formatting with an `strftime`inspired date and time formatting syntax.
- The `Local`
- Types and operations are implemented to be reasonably efficient.

Timezone data is not shipped with chrono by default to limit binary sizes. Use the companion crate
[Chrono-TZ](https://crates.io/crates/chrono-tz) or [ tzfile](https://crates.io/crates/tzfile) for
full timezone support.

## Documentation

See [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/) for the API reference.

## Limitations

- Only the proleptic Gregorian calendar (i.e. extended to support older dates) is supported.
- Date types are limited to about +/- 262,000 years from the common epoch.
- Time types are limited to nanosecond accuracy.
- Leap seconds can be represented, but Chrono does not fully support them.
See [Leap Second Handling](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/naive/struct.NaiveTime.html#leap-second-handling).

## Crate features

Default features:

- `alloc`: Enable features that depend on allocation (primarily string formatting).
- `std`: Enables functionality that depends on the standard library. This is a superset of- `alloc`and adds interoperation with standard library types and traits.
- `clock`: Enables reading the local timezone (- `Local`). This is a superset of- `now`.
- `now`: Enables reading the system time (- `now`).
- `wasmbind`: Interface with the JS Date API for the- `wasm32`target.

Optional features:

- `serde`: Enable serialization/deserialization via- [serde](https://github.com/serde-rs/serde).
- `rkyv`: Deprecated, use the- `rkyv-*`features.
- `rkyv-16`: Enable serialization/deserialization via- [rkyv](https://github.com/rkyv/rkyv), using 16-bit integers for integral- `*size`types.
- `rkyv-32`: Enable serialization/deserialization via- [rkyv](https://github.com/rkyv/rkyv), using 32-bit integers for integral- `*size`types.
- `rkyv-64`: Enable serialization/deserialization via- [rkyv](https://github.com/rkyv/rkyv), using 64-bit integers for integral- `*size`types.
- `rkyv-validation`: Enable rkyv validation support using- `bytecheck`.
- `arbitrary`: Construct arbitrary instances of a type with the Arbitrary crate.
- `unstable-locales`: Enable localization. This adds various methods with a- `_localized`suffix. The implementation and API may change or even be removed in a patch release. Feedback welcome.
- `oldtime`: This feature no longer has any effect; it used to offer compatibility with the- `time`0.1 crate.

Note: The `rkyv{,-16,-32,-64}` features are mutually exclusive.

## Rust version requirements

The Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV) is currently **Rust 1.62.0**.

The MSRV is explicitly tested in CI. It may be bumped in minor releases, but this is not done lightly.

# is-terminal 0.4.17 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/is-terminal/^0.4.7

As of Rust 1.70, most users should use the [ IsTerminal](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/io/trait.IsTerminal.html) trait in the Rust
standard library instead of this crate.

On Unix platforms, this crate now uses libc, so that the implementation
matches what's in std. Users wishing to use the rustix-based implementation
can use the [rustix-is-terminal](https://crates.io/crates/rustix-is-terminal) crate instead.

is-terminal is a simple utility that answers one question:

Is this a terminal?

A "terminal", also known as a "tty", is an I/O device which may be interactive and may support color and other special features. This crate doesn't provide any of those features; it just answers this one question.

On Unix-family platforms, this is effectively the same as the [ isatty](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/isatty.3.html)
function for testing whether a given stream is a terminal, though it accepts
high-level stream types instead of raw file descriptors.

On Windows, it uses a variety of techniques to determine whether the given stream is a terminal.

This crate is derived from [the atty crate](https://crates.io/crates/atty) with [PR #51](https://github.com/softprops/atty/pull/51) bug fix and
[PR #54](https://github.com/softprops/atty/pull/54) port to windows-sys applied. The only additional difference is that
the atty crate only accepts stdin, stdout, or stderr, while this crate accepts
any stream. In particular, this crate does not access any stream that is not
passed to it, in accordance with [I/O safety](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/master/text/3128-io-safety.md).

## Example

```
use IsTerminal;
```
## Testing

This library is tested on both Unix-family and Windows platforms.

To test it on a platform manually, use the provided `stdio` example program.
When run normally, it prints this:

# log 0.4.33 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/log/^0.4.11

# log

A Rust library providing a lightweight logging *facade*.

A logging facade provides a single logging API that abstracts over the actual logging implementation. Libraries can use the logging API provided by this crate, and the consumer of those libraries can choose the logging implementation that is most suitable for its use case.

## Minimum supported `rustc`

See the `rust-version` field in `Cargo.toml` for the current minimum Rust toolchain version.

This version is explicitly tested in CI and may be bumped in any release as needed. Maintaining compatibility with older compilers is a priority though, so the bar for bumping the minimum supported version is set very high. Any changes to the supported minimum version will be called out in the release notes.

## Usage

### In libraries

Libraries should link only to the `log` crate, and use the provided macros to
log whatever information will be useful to downstream consumers:

```
[]
 = "0.4"
```
```
use ;
```
### In executables

In order to produce log output, executables have to use a logger implementation compatible with the facade. There are many available implementations to choose from, here are some options:

- Simple minimal loggers:
- Complex configurable frameworks:
- Adaptors for other facilities:
- For WebAssembly binaries:
- For dynamic libraries:
- You may need to construct [an FFI-safe wrapper over](https://github.com/rust-lang/log/issues/421)to initialize in your libraries.`log`

- You may need to construct
- Utilities:

Executables should choose a logger implementation and initialize it early in the runtime of the program. Logger implementations will typically include a function to do this. Any log messages generated before the logger is initialized will be ignored.

The executable itself may use the `log` crate to log as well.

## Structured logging

If you enable the `kv` feature, you can associate structured data with your log records:

```
use ;
```

# termcolor 1.1.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/termcolor/~1.1

# termcolor

A simple cross platform library for writing colored text to a terminal. This library writes colored text either using standard ANSI escape sequences or by interacting with the Windows console. Several convenient abstractions are provided for use in single-threaded or multi-threaded command line applications.

Dual-licensed under MIT or the [UNLICENSE](https://unlicense.org/).

### Documentation

### Usage

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "1.1"
```
### Organization

The `WriteColor` trait extends the `io::Write` trait with methods for setting
colors or resetting them.

`StandardStream` and `StandardStreamLock` both satisfy `WriteColor` and are
analogous to `std::io::Stdout` and `std::io::StdoutLock`, or `std::io::Stderr`
and `std::io::StderrLock`.

`Buffer` is an in memory buffer that supports colored text. In a parallel
program, each thread might write to its own buffer. A buffer can be printed to
stdout or stderr using a `BufferWriter`. The advantage of this design is that
each thread can work in parallel on a buffer without having to synchronize
access to global resources such as the Windows console. Moreover, this design
also prevents interleaving of buffer output.

`Ansi` and `NoColor` both satisfy `WriteColor` for arbitrary implementors of
`io::Write`. These types are useful when you know exactly what you need. An
analogous type for the Windows console is not provided since it cannot exist.

### Example: using `StandardStream`

The `StandardStream` type in this crate works similarly to `std::io::Stdout`,
except it is augmented with methods for coloring by the `WriteColor` trait.
For example, to write some green text:

```
use ;
use ;
```
### Example: using `BufferWriter`

A `BufferWriter` can create buffers and write buffers to stdout or stderr. It
does *not* implement `io::Write` or `WriteColor` itself. Instead, `Buffer`
implements `io::Write` and `termcolor::WriteColor`.

This example shows how to print some green text to stderr.

```
use ;
use ;
```
### Automatic color selection

When building a writer with termcolor, the caller must provide a
[ ColorChoice](https://docs.rs/termcolor/1.*/termcolor/enum.ColorChoice.html)
selection. When the color choice is

`Auto`, termcolor will attempt to determine
whether colors should be enabled by inspecting the environment. Currently,
termcolor will inspect the `TERM` and `NO_COLOR` environment variables:- If `NO_COLOR`is set to any value, then colors will be suppressed.
- If `TERM`is set to`dumb`, then colors will be suppressed.
- In non-Windows environments, if `TERM`is not set, then colors will be suppressed.

This decision procedure may change over time.

Currently, `termcolor` does not attempt to detect whether a tty is present or
not. To achieve that, please use the [ atty](https://crates.io/crates/atty)
crate.

### Minimum Rust version policy

This crate's minimum supported `rustc` version is `1.34.0`.

The current policy is that the minimum Rust version required to use this crate
can be increased in minor version updates. For example, if `crate 1.0` requires
Rust 1.20.0, then `crate 1.0.z` for all values of `z` will also require Rust
1.20.0 or newer. However, `crate 1.y` for `y > 0` may require a newer minimum
version of Rust.

In general, this crate will be conservative with respect to the minimum supported version of Rust.

# thread_local

This library provides the `ThreadLocal` type which allow a separate copy of an
object to be used for each thread. This allows for per-object thread-local
storage, unlike the standard library's `thread_local!` macro which only allows
static thread-local storage.

# docopt 1.1.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/docopt/^1.1

# THIS CRATE IS UNMAINTAINED

This crate is unlikely to see significant future evolution. The primary reason
to choose this crate for a new project is if you're specifically interested in
using [docopt](http://docopt.org/) syntax for your project. However, the wider
docopt project is mostly unmaintained at this point.

Consider using [clap](http://docs.rs/clap/) or possibly
[structopt](http://docs.rs/structopt/) instead.

Note that this crate has some significant bugs. The two biggest ones are the
lack of `OsStr` support and some severe performance problems in not-uncommon
edge cases.

# docopt

Docopt for Rust with automatic type based decoding (i.e., data validation).
This implementation conforms to the
[official description of Docopt](http://docopt.org/) and
[passes its test suite](https://github.com/docopt/docopt/pull/201).

Dual-licensed under MIT or the [UNLICENSE](http://unlicense.org).

### Documentation

### Installation

This crate is fully compatible with Cargo. Just add it to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "1"
 = {  = "1",  = ["derive"] }
```
### Quick example

Here is a full working example. Notice that you can specify the types of each of the named values in the Docopt usage string. Values will be automatically converted to those types (or an error will be reported).

```
use Docopt;
use Deserialize;
const USAGE: &'static str = "
Naval Fate.
Usage:
  naval_fate.py ship new <name>...
  naval_fate.py ship <name> move <x> <y> [--speed=<kn>]
  naval_fate.py ship shoot <x> <y>
  naval_fate.py mine (set|remove) <x> <y> [--moored | --drifting]
  naval_fate.py (-h | --help)
  naval_fate.py --version
Options:
  -h --help     Show this screen.
  --version     Show version.
  --speed=<kn>  Speed in knots [default: 10].
  --moored      Moored (anchored) mine.
  --drifting    Drifting mine.
";
```
### Struct field name mapping

The field names of the struct map like this:

```
-g            => flag_g
--group       => flag_group
--group <arg> => flag_group
FILE          => arg_FILE
<file>        => arg_file
build         => cmd_build
```
### Traditional Docopt API

The reference implementation of Docopt returns a Python dictionary with names
like `<arg>` or `--flag`. If you prefer this access pattern, then you can use
`docopt::ArgvMap`. The disadvantage is that you have to do all of your type
conversion manually. Here's the canonical Docopt example with a hash table:

```
use Docopt;
const USAGE: &'static str = "
Naval Fate.
Usage:
  naval_fate.py ship new <name>...
  naval_fate.py ship <name> move <x> <y> [--speed=<kn>]
  naval_fate.py ship shoot <x> <y>
  naval_fate.py mine (set|remove) <x> <y> [--moored | --drifting]
  naval_fate.py (-h | --help)
  naval_fate.py --version
Options:
  -h --help     Show this screen.
  --version     Show version.
  --speed=<kn>  Speed in knots [default: 10].
  --moored      Moored (anchored) mine.
  --drifting    Drifting mine.
";
```
### Tab completion support

This particular implementation bundles a command called `docopt-wordlist` that
can be used to automate tab completion. This repository also collects some
basic completion support for various shells (currently only bash) in the
`completions` directory.

You can use them to setup tab completion on your system. It should work with
any program that uses Docopt (or rather, any program that outputs usage
messages that look like Docopt). For example, to get tab completion support for
Cargo, you'll have to install `docopt-wordlist` and add some voodoo to your
`$HOME/.bash_completion` file (this may vary for other shells).

Here it is step by step:

```
# Download and build `docopt-wordlist` (as part of the Docopt package)
# Now setup tab completion (for bash)
```
My [CSV toolkit](https://github.com/BurntSushi/xsv) is supported too:

```
# shameless plug...
```
Note that this is emphatically a first pass. There are several improvements that I'd like to make:

- Take context into account when completing. For example, it should be possible to only show completions that can lead to a valid Docopt match. This may be hard. (i.e., It may require restructuring Docopt's internals.)
- Support more shells. (I'll happily accept pull requests on this one. I doubt I'll venture outside of bash any time soon.)
- Make tab completion support more seamless. The way it works right now is pretty hacky by intermingling file/directory completion.

# libc 0.2.186 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/libc/^0.2.18

# libc - Raw FFI bindings to platforms' system libraries

`libc` provides all of the definitions necessary to easily interoperate with C
code (or "C-like" code) on each of the platforms that Rust supports. This
includes type definitions (e.g. `c_int`), constants (e.g. `EINVAL`) as well as
function headers (e.g. `malloc`).

This crate exports all underlying platform types, functions, and constants under
the crate root, so all items are accessible as `libc::foo`. The types and values
of all the exported APIs match the platform that libc is compiled for.

Windows API bindings are not included in this crate. If you are looking for
WinAPI bindings, consider using crates like [windows-sys](https://docs.rs/windows-sys).

More detailed information about the design of this library can be found in its
[associated RFC](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/HEAD/text/1291-promote-libc.md).

## v1.0 Roadmap

Currently, `libc` has two active branches: `main` for the upcoming v1.0 release,
and `libc-0.2` for the currently published version. By default all pull requests
should target `main`; once reviewed, they can be cherry picked to the `libc-0.2`
branch if needed.

We will stop making new v0.2 releases once v1.0 is released.

See the section in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://docs.rs/CONTRIBUTING.md#v10-roadmap) for more
details.

## Usage

Add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.2"
```
## Features

-
`std`: by default`libc`links to the standard library. Disable this feature to remove this dependency and be able to use`libc`in`#![no_std]`crates.
-
`extra_traits`: all`struct`s implemented in`libc`are`Copy`and`Clone`. This feature derives`Debug`,`Eq`,`Hash`, and`PartialEq`.

The following features are deprecated:

- `use_std`: this is equivalent to- `std`
- `const-extern-fn`: this is now enabled by default
- `align`: this is now enabled by default

## Rust version support

The minimum supported Rust toolchain version is currently **Rust 1.65**.

Increases to the MSRV are allowed to change without a major (i.e. semver- breaking) release in order to avoid a ripple effect in the ecosystem. A policy for when this may change is a work in progress.

`libc` may continue to compile with Rust versions older than the current MSRV
but this is not guaranteed.

## Platform support

You can see the platform(target)-specific docs on [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/libc), select a platform
you want to see.

See [ ci/verify-build.py](https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/blob/HEAD/ci/verify-build.py) for
the platforms on which

`libc` is guaranteed to build for each Rust toolchain.
The test matrices at [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/actions)show the platforms in which

`libc` tests
are run.## License

This project is licensed under either of

at your option.

We welcome all people who want to contribute. Please see the
[contributing instructions](https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information.

Contributions in any form (issues, pull requests, etc.) to this project must
adhere to Rust's [Code of Conduct](https://www.rust-lang.org/policies/code-of-conduct).

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted

# structopt 0.3.26 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/structopt/^0.3.20

# StructOpt

Parse command line arguments by defining a struct.  It combines [clap](https://crates.io/crates/clap) with custom derive.

## Maintenance

As clap v3 is now out, and the structopt features are integrated into (almost as-is), structopt is now in maintenance mode: no new feature will be added.

Bugs will be fixed, and documentation improvements will be accepted.

## Documentation

Find it on [Docs.rs](https://docs.rs/structopt).  You can also check the [examples](https://github.com/TeXitoi/structopt/tree/master/examples) and the [changelog](https://github.com/TeXitoi/structopt/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md).

## Example

Add `structopt` to your dependencies of your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.3"
```
And then, in your rust file:

```
use PathBuf;
use StructOpt;
/// A basic example
```
Using this example:

```
$ ./basic
error: The following required arguments were not provided:
    --output <output>
USAGE:
    basic --output <output> --speed <speed>
For more information try --help
$ ./basic --help
basic 0.3.0
Guillaume Pinot <texitoi@texitoi.eu>, others
A basic example
USAGE:
    basic [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] --output <output> [--] [file]...
FLAGS:
    -d, --debug      Activate debug mode
    -h, --help       Prints help information
    -V, --version    Prints version information
    -v, --verbose    Verbose mode (-v, -vv, -vvv, etc.)
OPTIONS:
    -l, --level <level>...     admin_level to consider
    -c, --nb-cars <nb-cars>    Number of cars
    -o, --output <output>      Output file
    -s, --speed <speed>        Set speed [default: 42]
ARGS:
    <file>...    Files to process
$ ./basic -o foo.txt
Opt {
    debug: false,
    verbose: 0,
    speed: 42.0,
    output: "foo.txt",
    nb_cars: None,
    level: [],
    files: [],
}
$ ./basic -o foo.txt -dvvvs 1337 -l alice -l bob --nb-cars 4 bar.txt baz.txt
Opt {
    debug: true,
    verbose: 3,
    speed: 1337.0,
    output: "foo.txt",
    nb_cars: Some(
        4,
    ),
    level: [
        "alice",
        "bob",
    ],
    files: [
        "bar.txt",
        "baz.txt",
    ],
}
```
## StructOpt rustc version policy

- Minimum rustc version modification must be specified in the [changelog](https://github.com/TeXitoi/structopt/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)and in the[travis configuration](https://github.com/TeXitoi/structopt/blob/master/.travis.yml).
- Contributors can increment minimum rustc version without any justification if the new version is required by the latest version of one of StructOpt's dependencies (`cargo update`will not fail on StructOpt).
- Contributors can increment minimum rustc version if the library user experience is improved.

# stderrlog - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/stderrlog

## Expand description

A simple logger to provide semantics similar to what is expected of most UNIX utilities by logging to stderr and the higher the verbosity the higher the log level. It supports the ability to provide timestamps at different granularities. As well as colorizing the different log levels.

[§](https://docs.rs#simple-use-case)Simple Use Case

```
use log::*;
fn main() {
    stderrlog::new().module(module_path!()).init().unwrap();
    error!("some failure");
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#structopt-example)StructOpt Example

```
use log::*;
use structopt::StructOpt;
/// A StructOpt example
#[derive(StructOpt, Debug)]
#[structopt()]
struct Opt {
    /// Silence all output
    #[structopt(short = "q", long = "quiet")]
    quiet: bool,
    /// Verbose mode (-v, -vv, -vvv, etc)
    #[structopt(short = "v", long = "verbose", parse(from_occurrences))]
    verbose: usize,
    /// Timestamp (sec, ms, ns, none)
    #[structopt(short = "t", long = "timestamp")]
    ts: Option<stderrlog::Timestamp>,
}
fn main() {
    let opt = Opt::from_args();
    stderrlog::new()
        .module(module_path!())
        .quiet(opt.quiet)
        .verbosity(opt.verbose)
        .timestamp(opt.ts.unwrap_or(stderrlog::Timestamp::Off))
        .init()
        .unwrap();
    trace!("trace message");
    debug!("debug message");
    info!("info message");
    warn!("warn message");
    error!("error message");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#docopt-example)docopt Example

```
use log::*;
use docopt::Docopt;
use serde::Deserialize;
const USAGE: &'static str = "
Usage: program [-q] [-v...]
";
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct Args {
    flag_q: bool,
    flag_v: usize,
}
fn main() {
    let args: Args = Docopt::new(USAGE)
                            .and_then(|d| d.deserialize())
                            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.exit());
    stderrlog::new()
            .module(module_path!())
            .quiet(args.flag_q)
            .timestamp(stderrlog::Timestamp::Second)
            .verbosity(args.flag_v)
            .init()
            .unwrap();
    trace!("trace message");
    debug!("debug message");
    info!("info message");
    warn!("warn message");
    error!("error message");
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#clap-example)clap Example

```
use clap::{Arg, App, crate_version};
use log::*;
use std::str::FromStr;
fn main() {
    let m = App::new("stderrlog example")
        .version(crate_version!())
        .arg(Arg::with_name("verbosity")
             .short('v')
             .takes_value(true)
             .multiple(true)
             .help("Increase message verbosity"))
        .arg(Arg::with_name("quiet")
             .short('q')
             .help("Silence all output"))
        .arg(Arg::with_name("timestamp")
             .short('t')
             .help("prepend log lines with a timestamp")
             .takes_value(true)
             .possible_values(&["none", "sec", "ms", "ns"]))
        .get_matches();
    let verbose = m.occurrences_of("verbosity") as usize;
    let quiet = m.is_present("quiet");
    let ts = m.value_of("timestamp").map(|v| {
        stderrlog::Timestamp::from_str(v).unwrap_or_else(|_| {
            clap::Error::raw(clap::ErrorKind::InvalidValue, "invalid value for 'timestamp'").exit()
        })
    }).unwrap_or(stderrlog::Timestamp::Off);
    stderrlog::new()
        .module(module_path!())
        .quiet(quiet)
        .verbosity(verbose)
        .timestamp(ts)
        .init()
        .unwrap();
    trace!("trace message");
    debug!("debug message");
    info!("info message");
    warn!("warn message");
    error!("error message");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#log-compatibility)`log` Compatibility

The 0.5.x versions of `stderrlog` aim to provide compatibility with
applications using `log` >= 0.4.11.

[§](https://docs.rs#rust-compatibility)Rust Compatibility

`stderrlog` is serious about backwards compat. `stderrlog`
pins the minimum required version of Rust in the CI build.
Bumping the minimum version of Rust is a minor breaking
change and requires a minor version to be bumped.

The minimum supported Rust version for this release is 1.48.0.

[§](https://docs.rs#module-level-logging)Module Level Logging

`stderrlog` has the ability to limit the components which can log.
Many crates use [log](https://docs.rs/log/*/log/) but you may not
want their output in your application. For example
[hyper](https://docs.rs/hyper/*/hyper/) makes heavy use of log but
when your application receives `-vvvvv` to enable the `trace!()`
messages you don’t want the output of `hyper`’s `trace!()` level.

To support this `stderrlog` includes a `module()` method allowing
you to specify the modules that are allowed to log. The examples
above use the `module_path!()` macro to enable logging only for
the binary itself but none of its dependencies. To enable logging
from extra crates just add another call to `module()` with the
name of the crate. To enable logging for only a module within
that crate specify `crate::module` to `module()`. crates and
modules will be named the same way would would include them in
source code with `use` (e.g. `some-crate` would be `some_crate`).

For a good example of how the module level logging works see the
[large-example
crate](https://github.com/cardoe/stderrlog-rs/tree/master/examples/large-example)
under examples, you’ll want to run the
following binaries to see all the examples:

- `cargo run --bin large-example --`
- `cargo run --bin another --`
- `cargo run --bin yet --`

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

`stderrlog` has the following default crate features, which can be disabled
to reduce the number of dependencies:

- `timestamps`: Provides support for log timestamp prefixes (uses the- `chrono`crate).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [StdErr](https://docs.rs/struct.StdErrLog.html)- Log
- Data specific to this logger

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Color](https://docs.rs/enum.ColorChoice.html)- Choice
- ColorChoice represents the color preferences of an end user.
- [LogLevel](https://docs.rs/enum.LogLevelNum.html)- Num
- [Timestamp](https://docs.rs/enum.Timestamp.html)
- State of the timestamping in the logger.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [new](https://docs.rs/fn.new.html)
- creates a new stderr logger

# stderrlog 0.6.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/stderrlog/latest/source/CHANGELOG.md

#ChangeLog##0.6.0###Changed-Bumped the minimum Rust version to 1.48.0
*[RUSTSEC-2021-0145](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2021-0145) fixed
##0.5.3###Changed-Moved the timestamps feature behind the enabled-by-default crate feature `timestamps`.
###Fixed-Added missing `show_module_names` field to `StdErrLog` debug implementation.
##0.5.2###Changed-Bumped the minimum Rust version to 1.36.0
*[RUSTSEC-2022-0006](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2022-0006.html) fixed
This is a semver break but given the age of the Rust versions and changes that have
happened in the log crate, we'll do it.
- Make it easier to specify debug levels with a number or enum.
##0.5.1###Added-added `.show_module_names()` to include module name in output
##0.5.0###Changed-Bumped minimum Rust version to 1.31.0
* 1.16.0 fails on current version of some deps and some crates.io fetches
* Log crate 0.4.11 raised its MSRV to 1.31.0
- Updated and checked minimum version of all deps
- Switched to rust edition 2018
- Improved CI testing
##0.4.3###Changed-only check if stderr is a tty for the auto color choice, all other
choices pass through without modification
- bump termcolor to 1.0
##0.4.2###Added-add the ability to not show logging levels via `.show_levels()`###Fixed-auto color choice (the default) will now disable colors if stderr
is not connected to a tty by default
##0.4.1###Added-Support millisecond timestamp resolution
##0.4.0###Added-Timestamp now implements FromStr to make arg parsers quicker to implement
- Added a StructOpt example to the crate documentation and examples
###Changed-Improved clap example and added Timestamp support
- Full use and depend on log 0.4.1.
##0.3.0###Added-a large example under examples to detail how module level logging
works
###Changed-bump minimum Rust version to 1.16.0
- allow all log 0.3.x releases
- fix situations where including `a::b` also included `a::baz`##0.2.4###Changed-pinned log to 0.3.8 or older to retain Rust 1.13.0 support
##0.2.3###Added-clap example
- support timestamps with microsecond and nanosecond granularity
###Changed-improved performance (https://github.com/cardoe/stderrlog-rs/pull/2)
- improved docopt example in README
- migrated from time to chrono
###Thanks-Thanks to Zachary Dremann <dremann@gmail.com> for the performance
improvements and the nudge to improve the docs.

Logger that aims to provide a simple case of
[env_logger](https://crates.io/crates/env_logger) that just
logs to `stderr` based on verbosity.
For a working example for [StructOpt](https::/crates.io/crates/structopt),
[clap](https://crates.io/crates/clap), and
[docopt](https://crates.io/crates/docopt) please see the
[crate level documentation](https://docs.rs/stderrlog/*/stderrlog/).
For example binaries showing how
[module level logging](https://github.com/cardoe/stderrlog-rs/tree/master/examples/large-example) works, please see the `large-example` crate in `examples/`.
* ****
Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:
```toml
[dependencies]
stderrlog = "0.4"
```
and this to your main():
```rust
stderrlog::new().verbosity(args.flag_v).quiet(args.flag_q).init().unwrap();
```
where your args struct is defined as:
```rust
struct Args {
}
```
```

# chrono 0.4.45 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/chrono/0.4.45

[Chrono](https://docs.rs/chrono): Timezone-aware date and time handling

Chrono aims to provide all functionality needed to do correct operations on dates and times in the
[proleptic Gregorian calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proleptic_Gregorian_calendar):

- The `DateTime`
- Operations that may produce an invalid or ambiguous date and time return `Option`or`MappedLocalTime`
- Configurable parsing and formatting with an `strftime`inspired date and time formatting syntax.
- The `Local`
- Types and operations are implemented to be reasonably efficient.

Timezone data is not shipped with chrono by default to limit binary sizes. Use the companion crate
[Chrono-TZ](https://crates.io/crates/chrono-tz) or [ tzfile](https://crates.io/crates/tzfile) for
full timezone support.

## Documentation

See [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/) for the API reference.

## Limitations

- Only the proleptic Gregorian calendar (i.e. extended to support older dates) is supported.
- Date types are limited to about +/- 262,000 years from the common epoch.
- Time types are limited to nanosecond accuracy.
- Leap seconds can be represented, but Chrono does not fully support them.
See [Leap Second Handling](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/naive/struct.NaiveTime.html#leap-second-handling).

## Crate features

Default features:

- `alloc`: Enable features that depend on allocation (primarily string formatting).
- `std`: Enables functionality that depends on the standard library. This is a superset of- `alloc`and adds interoperation with standard library types and traits.
- `clock`: Enables reading the local timezone (- `Local`). This is a superset of- `now`.
- `now`: Enables reading the system time (- `now`).
- `wasmbind`: Interface with the JS Date API for the- `wasm32`target.

Optional features:

- `serde`: Enable serialization/deserialization via- [serde](https://github.com/serde-rs/serde).
- `rkyv`: Deprecated, use the- `rkyv-*`features.
- `rkyv-16`: Enable serialization/deserialization via- [rkyv](https://github.com/rkyv/rkyv), using 16-bit integers for integral- `*size`types.
- `rkyv-32`: Enable serialization/deserialization via- [rkyv](https://github.com/rkyv/rkyv), using 32-bit integers for integral- `*size`types.
- `rkyv-64`: Enable serialization/deserialization via- [rkyv](https://github.com/rkyv/rkyv), using 64-bit integers for integral- `*size`types.
- `rkyv-validation`: Enable rkyv validation support using- `bytecheck`.
- `arbitrary`: Construct arbitrary instances of a type with the Arbitrary crate.
- `unstable-locales`: Enable localization. This adds various methods with a- `_localized`suffix. The implementation and API may change or even be removed in a patch release. Feedback welcome.
- `oldtime`: This feature no longer has any effect; it used to offer compatibility with the- `time`0.1 crate.

Note: The `rkyv{,-16,-32,-64}` features are mutually exclusive.

## Rust version requirements

The Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV) is currently **Rust 1.62.0**.

The MSRV is explicitly tested in CI. It may be bumped in minor releases, but this is not done lightly.

## License

This project is licensed under either of

at your option.

# arbitrary - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/arbitrary/^1.0.0/

## Expand description

The `Arbitrary` trait crate.

This trait provides an [ Arbitrary](https://docs.rs/trait.Arbitrary.html) trait to
produce well-typed, structured values, from raw, byte buffers. It is
generally intended to be used with fuzzers like AFL or libFuzzer. See the

[trait’s documentation for details on automatically deriving, implementing, and/or using the trait.](https://docs.rs/trait.Arbitrary.html)

`Arbitrary`## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [size_](https://docs.rs/size_hint/index.html)- hint
- Utilities for working with and combining the results of
`Arbitrary::size_hint`
- [unstructured](https://docs.rs/unstructured/index.html)
- Wrappers around raw, unstructured bytes.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [MaxRecursion](https://docs.rs/struct.MaxRecursionReached.html)- Reached
- Error indicating that the maximum recursion depth has been reached while calculating `Arbitrary::size_hint`
- [Unstructured](https://docs.rs/struct.Unstructured.html)
- A source of unstructured data.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- An enumeration of buffer creation errors

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Arbitrary](https://docs.rs/trait.Arbitrary.html)
- Generate arbitrary structured values from raw, unstructured data.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)
- A `Result`with the error type fixed as`arbitrary::Error`.

# defmt - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/defmt/^1.0.1/

## Expand description

A highly efficient logging framework that targets resource-constrained devices, like microcontrollers.

Check out the defmt book at [https://defmt.ferrous-systems.com](https://defmt.ferrous-systems.com) for more
information about how to use it.

[§](https://docs.rs#compatibility)Compatibility

The `defmt` wire format might change between minor versions. Attempting to
read a defmt stream with an incompatible version will result in an error,
and any tool used to process that stream should first check for a symbol
named like `_defmt_version_ = X`, where X indicates the wire format version
in use.

Updating your version of defmt might mean you also have to update your
version of `defmt-print` or `defmt-decoder`.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)
